title: intake --file --hook files nothing in a worker's linked worktree and says so on stderr
goal: backlog.py intake --file --hook, run in a linked git worktree under .claude/worktrees/ (a headless worker's), files no draft item and prints one line on stderr naming the worktree as the reason; in the main checkout it files as before and prints nothing. Answers the SP-sz5fbvqn retrospective: each worker session's SessionStart hook filed 5-6 untracked drafts under kb/_self/backlog/ of its worktree, one worker swept them into a commit with git add -A, and the orchestrator moved them aside before every land.

run: import tempfile,subprocess,sys,os;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();g=lambda *a,c=d:subprocess.run(['git','-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t@t','-C',c,*a],capture_output=True,text=True);g('init','-q');g('commit','-q','--allow-empty','-m','x');w=d+'/.claude/worktrees/w1';g('worktree','add','-q','-b','b1',w);os.makedirs(w+'/kb/_self/backlog',exist_ok=True);p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,os.getcwd()+'/_tools/backlog.py','--root',w,'intake','--file','--hook'],capture_output=True,text=True);ok=p.returncode==0 and 'worktree' in p.stderr;print('intake exit',p.returncode,'stderr:',p.stderr.strip() or 'empty','| says it files nothing in a worker worktree:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
